stories.summary: An international study found that a routine blood test can predict Alzheimer's-related cognitive decline up to ten years before symptoms manifest. Researchers hope the early detection method will enable timely medical interventions.
stories.title: A simple blood test could reveal Alzheimer’s risk 10 years before symptoms

stories.summary: A recent study revealed that dogs possess an innate ability to detect seizure scents from unfamiliar humans without prior training. The findings suggest canines naturally recognize chemical cues associated with medical episodes.
stories.title: Dogs May Smell a Complete Stranger's Seizure Without Ever Being Trained, Study Finds

stories.summary: Scientists at the University of Guelph are working to reintroduce the extirpated frosted elfin butterfly to its historical habitat in Ontario. The species was last documented in the province along Lake Erie in 1988.
stories.title: University of Guelph scientist working to return extirpated frosted elfin butterfly to Ontario

stories.summary: The annual Night Light Walk raised $24,800 to support services provided by Guelph-Wellington Women in Crisis. The event also helped build public awareness around housing needs and intimate partner violence prevention.
stories.title: Night Light Walk raises $24,800 for G-W Women in Crisis

stories.summary: Scientists at Johns Hopkins uncovered how the common gut bacterium Bacteroides fragilis can trigger colorectal cancer. Their research shows the bacterium produces a toxin that damages the colon's protective lining and promotes chronic inflammation.
stories.title: Scientists finally discover how a common gut bacterium can trigger colon cancer

stories.summary: Two 88-year-old retirees who had lost their long-term partners fell in love after meeting at a retirement village gym. The widowed couple recently celebrated finding unexpected companionship and romance.
stories.title: Retirees Who Lost Spouses Fall in Love Again at 88, After Meeting in the Gym

stories.summary: Archaeologists in Morocco discovered a 4,000-year-old defensive wall that reveals new insights into prehistoric North African societies. The massive fortifications demonstrate that ancient civilizations in the region were significantly more sophisticated than previously understood.
stories.title: A mysterious 4,000-year-old wall is rewriting North Africa’s history

stories.summary: Researchers discovered two experimental metal alloys that resist cracking at extremely low temperatures down to -424°F. The materials reorganize their internal structures under stress, allowing them to remain flexible rather than becoming brittle.
stories.title: Scientists discover metals that defy the deep freeze at -424°F

stories.summary: Researchers discovered a novel bacterial defense mechanism that operates in reverse compared to standard immune systems. The system activates lethal DNA only after a viral attack occurs, causing the infected cell to destroy itself to protect the colony.
stories.title: Scientists discover a bacterial defense so strange they thought it was broken

stories.summary: Johns Hopkins University researchers uncovered a process involving a vitamin A derivative and thyroid hormones that helps shape the human foveola before birth. Using lab-grown miniature retinas, the discovery challenges long-held assumptions about how vision develops.
stories.title: A surprising vitamin A discovery is changing what scientists know about vision

stories.summary: Physicists successfully recreated primordial matter from the early universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at near-light speeds. The experiment demonstrated that this exotic state of matter can form under lower energy conditions than previously thought.
stories.title: Scientists smash oxygen nuclei to recreate matter from the Big Bang

stories.summary: A scientist at the University of Guelph is leading a conservation project to restore the frosted elfin butterfly in Ontario. The species has not been documented in the province since 1988.
stories.title: University of Guelph scientist leads project to recover butterfly species in Ontario

stories.summary: The City of Guelph is expanding its water and wastewater treatment capacity to support future development. Municipal leaders note that expanded infrastructure is essential before further growth can occur.
stories.title: City expanding water treatment capacity to allow for growth

stories.summary: A prominent OB-GYN group has published updated guidance for managing hot flashes and other menopause symptoms. The new recommendations provide modern strategies to address sleep and body changes.
stories.title: There’s new guidance on menopause symptoms like hot flashes. What women need to know

stories.summary: A former steel factory in Pittsburgh has been redeveloped into a creative hub known as Mill 19. The project revitalizes a post-industrial site into a functional community space.
stories.title: Mill 19: a creative hub built into a former steel factory

stories.summary: New waste bins featuring underground storage capacity are being installed in downtown Guelph. The project is part of the city's Downtown Infrastructure Renewal Program to control street trash.
stories.title: Designed to hide excess trash, new waste bins coming to downtown

stories.summary: Toronto Pearson Airport has partnered with Seneca Polytechnic to connect students with local jobs. The initiative focuses on employment in aviation, operations, construction, and administration.
stories.title: Toronto Pearson airport, Seneca Polytechnic form partnership to connect students with in-demand jobs

stories.summary: A father describes how a family dinner game helped him connect Halloween with community generosity. His reflection emphasizes support for local charity efforts like the Santa Claus Fund.
stories.title: How a family dinner game helped me see the Christmas spirit in Halloween

stories.summary: Homeowners on Toronto's Pape Avenue have created elaborate, large-scale skeleton decorations for Halloween. The neighborhood display has drawn attention for its creative seasonal spirit.
stories.title: Is this Toronto's spookiest street? Meet the skeleton's of Pape Avenue

stories.summary: British-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid was born 76 years ago today and was knighted for her revolutionary architectural designs. Her firm continues to innovate and build upon her contributions to world architecture.
stories.title: Good News in History, October 31

stories.summary: An art exhibition in Bremen, Germany, is showcasing the historical role of dachshunds in art. Gallery visitors are invited to bring their own dogs to view the display.
stories.title: The dachshund is the muse in an exhibition showcasing the sausage dog’s history in art

stories.summary: Laboratory tests show that a traditional Chinese medicine formula can eliminate drug-resistant cancer cells. Researchers are investigating the compound to understand its potential clinical applications.
stories.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Formula Kills Drug-Resistant Cancer Cells in The Lab

stories.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day website features daily educational images of the universe. Each entry includes a photograph accompanied by an explanation written by a professional astronomer.
stories.title: APOD: 2026 October 31 – Night on a Spooky Planet

stories.summary: Scientists have built a robot dog controlled by biological human brain cells. The research explores using living neurons rather than artificial intelligence for robotic movement.
stories.title: Scientists Have Built a Robot Dog Powered by Human Brain Cells

stories.summary: McMaster researchers have identified a new vulnerability in the bacteria responsible for tuberculosis. The discovery targets the resilient organism's complex DNA repair mechanisms.
stories.title: McMaster discovery points to new weakness in the bacteria behind tuberculosis

stories.summary: Japan's northern island of Hokkaido has achieved its best potato harvest in a decade. Ideal temperatures and rainfall produced a banner crop despite widespread agricultural challenges elsewhere.
stories.title: Best Spud Harvest in a Decade Clears the Gloom of Crops Failing from Scorching Summer

stories.summary: Canada is joining a European supercomputer program as part of a broad partnership with the EU. The collaboration focuses on shared technological priorities.
stories.title: Canada to join European supercomputer program, collaborate on tech priorities

stories.summary: Two Brock University software engineering students are making an early impact in their industry. The partnership aims to accelerate career growth for graduate students.
stories.title: Industry partnership accelerates grad students’ career growth

stories.summary: A battery researcher won Canada's biggest science prize. The show also explores how space travel affects astronaut bones and looks at other scientific findings.
stories.title: How going to space ages astronaut bones, and more…

stories.summary: A charity founded by business leaders held an investment pitch event to support children's mental health. The conference is expected to raise millions of dollars for the cause.
stories.title: Pitching in: Charity founded by Bay Street businessmen holds pitchfest to support kids’ mental health

stories.summary: A McMaster researcher shares his passion for bats through ongoing lab work and public meet-and-bat events. His research helps shed new light on these creatures of the night.
stories.title: Bat signals: Research sheds light on creatures of the night

stories.summary: A new Diwali Discovery Box has brought festive items to the Guelph Farmers' Market. The special collection features local textiles, soaps, and candles.
stories.title: Diwali Discovery Box Brings a Bright Light to the Guelph Farmers' Market

stories.summary: Researchers successfully extended the lifespan of aging mice by 17% through blocking a single enzyme. The intervention brought multiple health benefits to the subjects.
stories.title: Blocking One Enzyme Extended Lifespan in Aging Mice by 17%

stories.summary: McMaster University recently hosted an international conference focused on plague research. Top global experts gathered to collaboratively answer pressing questions about the disease and its bacteria.
stories.title: World’s top plague experts meet at McMaster

stories.summary: The hit Broadway musical The Book of Mormon is returning to Centre in the Square in Kitchener next March. The successful production originally debuted in 2011.
stories.title: Broadway musical ‘The Book of Mormon’ returning to Centre in the Square

stories.summary: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk shared his emotional experience looking at Earth during a seven-hour spacewalk. He noted that the view fundamentally changed him.
stories.title: A spacewalk to remember: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk says seeing Earth 'changed' him

stories.summary: A distinguished Brock University graduate is recognized for his dedication to educational empowerment. Dr. Narine Dat Sookram uses education to advocate and create opportunities for others.
stories.title: Distinguished grad driven by transformative power of education

stories.summary: Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk participated in a seven-hour spacewalk outside the space station. He shared that viewing Earth from space was a deeply emotional and transformative experience.
stories.title: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk says seeing Earth during spacewalk 'changed' him

stories.summary: United Way Guelph Wellington Dufferin hosted its inaugural Top 7 Over 70 Awards celebration. The event recognized and celebrated local community changemakers for their contributions.
stories.title: Red Carpet: See who took centre stage at the Top 7 Over 70 Awards

stories.summary: Retired chef Bob Bignell has launched the Feed a Family of Four initiative to help local households. The project includes a website that aims to simplify grocery shopping for families in Fergus.
stories.title: New website making grocery shopping easier for Fergus families

stories.summary: A new study reveals that more than half of younger adults with type 2 diabetes achieved remission within six months. The success was driven by a low-calorie diet and structured exercise.
stories.title: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months

stories.summary: Italian police used artificial intelligence to help identify millions of dollars worth of stolen art and antiquities. The technology aids in recovering cultural heritage.
stories.title: Italian Police Used AI to Identify $200 M. Worth of Stolen Art and Antiquities

stories.summary: Women-led microenterprises in south-central Nepal are empowering local communities while promoting regional conservation efforts. Sustainable economic projects, such as traditional yarn spinning, provide income and foster local community development.
stories.title: Given a chance, women-led microenterprises uplift Nepali communities & conservation

stories.summary: Biologists are actively working to restore mangrove habitats in Mexico. The initiative helps revive local ecosystems and wildlife.
stories.title: Aztec methods and crocodiles: How biologists are restoring mangroves in Mexico

stories.summary: Citizen scientists in Pune are mapping local trees to help promote a greener urban future. Community members are directly contributing to environmental conservation.
stories.title: How citizen scientists are mapping Pune’s trees, with hopes of a greener future

stories.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope captured a detailed mid-infrared image of the Cat's Head Nebula. The image reveals intricate stellar structures sculpted over time by ultraviolet radiation and intense winds from nearby stars.
stories.title: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope Captures Eerie Cat’s Head

stories.summary: An annual witch-themed Halloween display on Birmingham Street West is drawing attention in Mount Forest. The festive neighborhood installation brings seasonal enjoyment to local residents.
stories.title: Annual witch-themed Halloween display turning heads in Mount Forest

stories.summary: A Texas school district named a new school after Marilyn Hampton, a longtime janitor. She received the honor in recognition of her decades of service as a custodian.
stories.title: New Texas School Is Named For Longtime Janitor ‘Miss Marilyn’ (Watch Her Reaction)

stories.summary: Nepal is testing artificial scent marking to keep big cats away from villages. This method helps prevent conflicts between humans and wildlife safely.
stories.title: After Botswana, Nepal tries artificial scent marking to fend big cats off villages

stories.summary: The province is investing $540,000 into a three-year research partnership with the University of Waterloo. This collaboration aims to develop new tools and technology to improve flood management and community resilience.
stories.title: Province partners with UW in effort to improve flood response and resilience
